title: SuperFast: Fast Supernet Training Using Initial Knowledge
problem: Once-for-all neural architecture search supernet training requires extremely high computational cost (72-83+ GPU days), limiting practical applicability despite enabling efficient multi-target deployment.
motivation: Prior acceleration attempts warm up the largest model in the search space, but smaller-to-larger knowledge transfer is more efficient than downward scaling.
method: SuperFast employs two-stage training: (1) pretrains a small subnet within the supernet search space, (2) distributes this subnet's learned knowledge across the full supernet before main training. Knowledge propagation from small to large models enables faster convergence and better accuracy-cost tradeoffs. Plug-and-play workflow compatible with ElasticViT and NASViT.
key_novelty: Knowledge distillation from small to large within once-for-all framework, reversing the conventional largest-model warmup approach.
contributions: SuperFast framework achieving 1.4x faster training on ElasticViT supernet at baseline accuracy
4.0 percentage point accuracy improvement at 20-50ms latency range on Pixel 6 mobile deployment
limitations: Evaluation on ImageNet and Pixel 6; generalization to other search spaces, datasets, or hardware platforms not explored.
primary_theme: Efficient supernet training via knowledge propagation
